log: LOOP 194  IS THE REGULATORY INPUT TO METABOLISM TIME-STRUCTURED?
PREDECLARED: flux balance is steady-state BY CONSTRUCTION, so this loop does not and
cannot put metabolism in 4D. It asks one link upstream, whether enzymes working on the
same chemistry are switched on together in time. There is NO measured flux time course
on this disk and transcript is not flux, so a pass means the regulatory INPUT is
coordinated and must not be quoted as though flux were. The grouping comes from the
model's own metabolite sharing with hubs excluded at degree > 50; V2 gates on
the graph not being near-complete, V4 repeats at other thresholds, V5 checks a curated
grouping independently, and V6 repeats everything against a null stratified by baseline
expression. Every coherence gate is z > 3.0 against 1000 permutations.

V7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
TRANSCRIPT IS NOT FLUX, and this is the limit that matters. An enzyme can be
transcribed without being translated, translated without being active, and active
without carrying flux. Metabolic control analysis exists because flux is usually not
set by any one enzyme's level. Nothing here licenses a claim about flux dynamics.
Flux balance remains steady-state by construction. Whatever this loop finds, the
solver in this project still cannot represent a trajectory, so a pass describes the
INPUT to a layer that has no time axis of its own.
One stimulus in one cell line, and a glucocorticoid response is not a metabolic
perturbation. Enzymes may be coordinated here because GR happens to hit them
together, which is a fact about dexamethasone rather than about metabolism.
Metabolite sharing is not pathway membership. Two enzymes joined by an uncommon
metabolite may sit in different subsystems, and the degree cut that removes H+ and
ATP is a threshold, not a definition of what counts as currency.
The response time is loop 196's incumbent statistic, which that loop measured to be
sound on this eleven-point grid and unusable below about eight points. Nothing here
extends to a coarser series.
